6243.t: Unknown, perhaps Pre-Greek. Probably cognate, ancestor, or descendant of Latin calx (“limestone, chalk”).

6244.t: Likely related to χαῦνος (khaûnos, “porous, loose-grained”) (via an earlier form χάος (kháos) < *χάϝος (*kháwos)), with original meaning "hole, empty space, yawning opening"; from this spring the traditional connections with χάσκω (kháskō, “to gape,…

6223.t: A variant of φυλή (phūlḗ, “tribe”), itself related to φύω (phúō, “to beget”).

6287.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂mélǵti, from *h₂melǵ- (“to milk”). Cognates include Latin mulgeō, Old English meolc (English milk), Gothic 𐌼𐌹𐌻𐌿𐌺𐍃 (miluks), and Albanian mjel.

6237.t: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰerH- (“bowel”), but the exact formation is unclear.

6228.t: From χαμαί (khamaí, “on the ground”) + λέων (léōn, “lion”); ultimately a calque of Akkadian 𒌨𒈤𒊭𒆠 (nēšu ša qaqqari, “chameleon, reptile”, literally “lion of the ground", "predator that crawls upon the ground”).

6200.t: From φαντός (phăntós, “visible”) + -άζω (-ắzō), verbal adjective of φαίνω (phaínō, “I cause to appear, bring to light”).

6233.t: Of unclear origin. Traditionally connected with χηραμός (khērămós, “hole, hollow”), χήμη (khḗmē, “yawning, gaping”), and χάσκω (kháskō, “to yawn, gape”), but the supposed unifying connections are obscure.

6251.t: If it dissimilated from *ψυθυρ-, it may belong to ψύθος (psúthos, “lie, untruth”). On the other hand, it can be compared to ψίζομαι (psízomai, “to weep”).

6204.t: Nominal form of the verb φθέγγομαι (phthéngomai, “to utter a sound, raise one's voice”).

6214.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰrakʷjō, of unclear origin, with analysis complicated by the coexistence and apparent confluence of φρακ- (phrak-) and φαρκ- (phark-) in the verb's derivatives.

6273.t: From an uncertain source apparently shared with Sanskrit अक्तु (aktú, “beam, ray”), perhaps: * Proto-Indo-European *h₂ekt- (“beam”), from an unidentified root; * Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp point”), which would exclude the Sanskrit; *…

6253.t: ἀ- (a-, “not”, alpha privativum) + βουλή (boulḗ, “will, determination, decision”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, abstract-noun-forming suffix)

6241.t: Apparently from a Proto-Indo-European *gʰreh₁-, *ǵʰreh₁- (“to desire, need”), with relation to other roots uncertain.

6245.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʰumə, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéwmn̥, from *ǵʰew- (“to pour”), whence χέω (khéō).

6203.t: From the root of φθέγγομαι (phthéngomai, “to make a sound”) + -μα (-ma).

6284.t: As if from *ἄμνητος (ámnētos) ("forgetful") + -ία (-íā), from ἀ- (a-) + μιμνήσκω (mimnḗskō) + -τος (-tos).

6217.t: From Proto-Indo-European *bʰerǵ- ~ *bʰreǵ- (“to roast, fry”), though the phonetics are irregular, suggesting a loanword from a third unidentified party.

6226.t: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew חֶלְבְּנָה (ḥɛlbənɔ̂), from the root ח־ל־ב (ḥ-l-b) related to milk, from Proto-Semitic *ḥalīb- (“milk; fat”).

6259.t: From ἀδάμας, ἀ˘δαμαντ- (adámās, ădămănt-, “diamond; steel”) + -ινος (-ĭnos, suffix).

6275.t: Presumably from λάω (láō, “to see”), although a privative formation should have barytone accentuation.

6219.t: From φυσάω (phūsáō, “to blow”) + -τήρ (-tḗr, agent noun suffix).

6210.t: From the Pre-Greek root *φλυκτ- (*phlŭkt-) + -ις (-ĭs). Compare φλύκταινα (phlŭ́ktaină, “blister”).

6269.t: From ἀ- (ă-, not; without) + κλέω (kléō, “to make famous”) + -ής (-ḗs, adjective suffix).
